Blood Products Plasma Expanders and Haemostatics 1042 Haematopoiesis, p.1042 Anaemias, p.1042 Aplastic anaemia, p.1042 Haemolytic anaemia, p.1043 Iron-deficiency anaemia, p.1044 Megaloblastic anaemia, p.1044 Normocytic-normochromic anaemia, p.1044 Sideroblastic anaemia, p.1044 Haemoglobinopathies, p.1044 Sickle-cell disease, p.1044 β-Thalassaemia, p.1045 Haemostasis and Fibrinolysis, p.1045 Acquired haemorrhagic disorders, p.1047 Disseminated intravascular coagulation, p.1048 Haemophilias, p.1048 Inherited haemorrhagic disorders, p.1050 Neonatal intraventricular haemorrhage, p.1050 Thrombocytopenia, p.1051 von Willebrand’s disease, p.1051 Neutropenia, p.1051 This chapter describes the management of blood disor- ders including some anaemias, haemorrhagic disor- ders, and neutropenia. It covers blood, blood products and substitutes, and colloid plasma expanders; crystal- loid plasma expanders are generally solutions of sodi- um chloride (p.1686) or glucose (p.1945) or both. Also included in the chapter are haemostatic drugs and erythropoietin and other colony-stimulating factors. The management of haematological malignancies is covered in the Antineoplastics chapter, p.635. Haematopoiesis In the embryo and fetus, the formation and develop- ment of blood cells occurs at various sites including the liver, spleen, thymus, lymph nodes, and bone marrow; from birth throughout the rest of life it occurs mainly in the bone marrow with a small amount occurring in the lymph nodes. The bone marrow contains pluripotent stem cells that differentiate into different types of pro- genitor cells (committed stem cells); these then mature into various types of blood cells under the influence of growth factors and hormones.
